title: Peer Check — Ask — payload
description: The request payload of peer-check/ask: a short yes-or-no question one party puts to another, with an unguessable challenge. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. The asker is the `issuer`, the party being asked is the `recipient`, and the document MUST carry `expiresAt`.

challenge.description: An unguessable value the asker generates for this one question: at least 128 bits from a cryptographically secure random source, encoded base64url without padding (22 to 86 characters). The responder echoes it unchanged in its answer.

question.description: What the asker wants confirmed, in one short sentence, for example "Did you just ask me to send you a one-time code?". It is asker-authored text the responder's device displays attributed to the asker, never as a statement the device itself vouches for.

note.description: OPTIONAL extra context from the asker. It is UNTRUSTED display text: the responder's device MUST render it as plain text, attributed to the asker and visually distinct from anything the device itself asserts, and MUST NOT interpret it as markup, a link, or an instruction.

Response.title: Peer Check Ask Response Payload
Response.description: The success-response payload: the responder's answer, signed by the responder. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape. A responder that declines because it does not recognise the question answers with `decision: denied`; an error is for a document the responder could not act on at all.

challenge.description: The `challenge` of the request, echoed unchanged. The asker rejects an answer whose challenge it did not issue, or has already consumed.

requestDigest.description: The task digest (SPEC §4.9.3) of the request document this answers: multibase(multihash(H(JCS(request without its top-level proof)))). It binds the answer to the exact question, challenge, note, parties and expiry the responder was shown, so a yes given to one ask cannot be presented as a yes to another.

decision.description: The responder's answer. `approved` means yes to the question as asked; `denied` means no.

respondedAt.description: When the responder gave the answer, RFC 3339. Informational for the asker; freshness is judged against the request's `expiresAt` and the asker's own clock.

deniedReason.description: OPTIONAL, and only meaningful with `decision: denied`; an asker MUST ignore it, and a responder MUST NOT send it, with `approved` (the schema does not enforce this). `notRecognised` — the responder does not recognise what the question describes; `declined` — the responder recognises it and says no; `other` — anything else. An enumeration rather than prose, so an asker never renders responder-authored text.
